10.1002_adfm.76943: Thin‐film composite (TFC) membranes with superior separation performance are widely applied in membrane separation technology. However, the selective layer in traditional TFC membranes is limited by uncontrollable fabrication processes and structural defects, constraining the further enhancement of their selectivity and permeability. Introducing nanomaterials with two‐dimensional (2D) nanochannels as functional platforms into TFC membranes can regulate the fabrication process of the selective layer and optimize membrane separation performance. This review proposes the concept of 2D material functional platforms (2DMFP) and focuses on the effects of 2DMFP on the structure and performance of TFC membranes, such as regulating processes including interfacial polymerization, orientation induction, and in situ growth of the selective layer in TFC membranes. Additionally, the application progress of TFC membranes with 2DMFP (2DMFP‐TFC membranes) in desalination, wastewater treatment, and gas separation is discussed. Finally, the challenges and future research directions of 2DMFP‐TFC membranes are analyzed, aiming to provide new insights for the design and application of high‐performance separation membranes.
10.1002_anie.5495010: Wide‐bandgap (WBG) perovskite solar cells (PSCs) are crucial for high‐efficiency tandem photovoltaics. However, their performance is severely limited by lattice disorder at the buried interface, which leads to the accumulation of deep‐level defects and interfacial morphological inhomogeneities, thereby inducing pronounced non‐radiative recombination and halide segregation. Here, we report a copper (II) chloride (CuCl 2 ) mediated interfacial permeation strategy that achieves the redox mediation and halide coordination, thereby stabilizing the interfacial chemical state, suppressing the formation of deep‐level defects. The strategy effectively suppresses lattice disorder at the buried interface, while simultaneously constructing an efficient hole‐transfer structure, thus enhancing interfacial phase stability and charge‐transport properties. Consequently, our modified 1.79 eV WBG PSCs exhibit minimized non‐radiative recombination losses and superior charge transport, achieving state‐of‐the‐art performance with an open circuit voltage ( V OC ) of 1.35 V, a fill factor of 84.29%, and power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 21.24%, one of the highest reported so far. The device can maintain 91% of its original efficiency after 1400 h of maximum power point tracking.
10.1002_smll.76495: Microsized Si/C composite anodes are promising for practical lithium‐ion batteries due to their high tap density and scalability. However, their performance remains constrained by structural degradation and an unstable solid electrolyte interface (SEI), and current strategies fail to address the intrinsic coupling between interfacial chemistry and Li + transport kinetics. Here, a structure‐interface co‐engineered microspherical Mo/W@Gr–Si anode is developed by integrating a flower‐like graphene framework with Mo 2 N/W 2 C dual‐phase heterostructures, enabling simultaneous regulation of Li + adsorption and diffusion. Coupled density functional theory (DFT) calculations and advanced characterizations reveal a mechanism linking interfacial stabilization with Li + transport, where the Mo 2 N/W 2 C heterophase stabilizes an inorganic‐rich SEI and reduces diffusion barriers via electronic structure modulation. Consequently, the Mo/W@Gr–Si anode exhibits a low Li + adsorption energy (−2.071 eV) and a reduced diffusion barrier (0.42 eV), delivering a high reversible capacity of 1821 mAh g − 1 at 0.1C with an initial coulombic efficiency of 88.12%, along with outstanding rate capability and cycling stability. Full cell paired with an NCM523 cathode retains 88.2% capacity after 300 cycles (0.5C), while pouch cells exhibit 84.6% retention after 200 cycles at 2C. This work offers a generalizable strategy for bridging interfacial stability and Li + transport kinetics in high‐performance silicon anodes.
10.1016_j.memsci.2026.125644: Operating electrodialysis (ED) processes beyond the limiting current density offers the potential for reduced capital costs and improved energy efficiency, but is fundamentally constrained by concentration polarization and the associated increase in electrical resistance. Spacer geometries are commonly employed to manipulate hydrodynamics in ED channels and enhance mass transfer. However, their impact on overlimiting ion transport remains insufficiently understood. In this study, we systematically investigate how specifically designed spacer geometries influence limiting and overlimiting current behavior by coupling electrochemical measurements with three-dimensional computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations. Custom spacer structures were fabricated by 3D printing and evaluated using current–voltage (I–V) characteristics and chronopotentiometric measurements under buoyancy-stable and buoyancy-unstable configurations. The simulations resolve spacer-induced flow fields, near-membrane shear distributions, ion transport, and current-density patterns, enabling direct correlation with experimental performance. While all spacer geometries enhance average mass transfer compared to a spacerless reference, their electrochemical effectiveness strongly depends on the spatial overlap between regions of increased near-membrane shear and electrically active membrane area. Spacer designs that generate strong local mixing but simultaneously induce electric-field shadowing lead to highly non-uniform current distributions, early local ion depletion, and modest gains in effective limiting and overlimiting currents. In contrast, geometries that promote a more homogeneous alignment of shear enhancement and electric driving force delay concentration polarization and stabilize overlimiting operation, particularly under buoyancy-stable conditions where forced convection dominates. These findings allow us to rationalize why spacer geometries that perform well in terms of classical mass-transfer metrics do not necessarily translate into improved overlimiting electrodialysis performance.
10.1021_jacs.6c10847: Contact-electrification (CE) is a ubiquitous effect that would render two contact surfaces being reversely charged. These charged surfaces would induce an electric field in space, but polarization caused by this CE-derived electric field has long been ignored. Here, we propose an electrostatic polarization strategy to improve the performance of single-atom catalysts (SACs) based on this CE-derived electric field. Exemplified by Ru 1 /SiO 2, its hydrogen yield could be enhanced by 7.62 times after improving the CE ability of the SiO 2 substrate by fluorination. Such enhancement should mainly be ascribed to the expedited CE effect on fluorinated SiO 2 substrates, which not only facilitates the water dissociation process but also establishes a strong electric field for improving the reduction activity of Ru SAs and the electrostatic attraction of protons. In addition, this strategy is feasible for SACs based on carbon substrates, further suggesting its generalizability. The practicability of Ru 1 /F-SiO 2 was demonstrated through hydrogen evolution from real seawater, achieving a yield of 1.01 mmol·g –1 ·h –1 over 200 h. We expect this electrostatic polarization-based strategy to form a universal route for enhancing the activity of SACs.
10.1039_d6ta04271f: This review explains how CQD–MOF interfacial chemistry controls charge transfer, ROS generation, and persistent organic pollutant degradation. It establishes design and validation criteria for sustainable photocatalysis.
